rules.quote: You must have someone’s explicit permission to add them to a mailing list and you must give them the option to unsubscribe.
rules.violation_condition: adding a person to a mailing list without explicit permission, or failing to provide an option to unsubscribe
rules.why: Strict obligation under Spam Act / privacy guidance (G-2).

rules.quote: Include the recipient’s name and postal address at the top of the letter.
rules.violation_condition: a letter missing the recipient's name and postal address at the top
rules.why: Specific, checkable rule for formatting letter address blocks (G-4).

rules.quote: With emails, explain in the covering text that the email has a letter attached.
rules.violation_condition: an email with an attached letter that does not explain in the covering text that a letter is attached
when: An email has a letter attached.
rules.why: Clear textual instruction for covering emails.

rules.quote: Include the date you are sending the letter so that the recipient knows when you wrote it.
rules.violation_condition: a letter that omits the date it is sent
rules.why: Standard formatting requirement for correspondence.

covers.quote: Write a clear and concise subject line
Avoid using expressions and words that make the email look like spam or like a suspicious email.
A subject in a letter is like a subject line in an email. It’s what the recipient will read first and must make the purpose of the letter very clear.

parts.quote: Items of interest for possible discussion by the Working Group on Safety in Melbourne next month

rules.quote: Be clear and concise with the subject line. It should sum up the purpose of the email.
rules.specification: Subject lines should put the main idea first, be concise, and avoid spam-like or overly wordy phrasing.
rules.violation_condition: an email subject line or letter subject that does not state the purpose clearly and concisely, such as being vague, overly verbose, or looking like spam
rules.why: Consolidates rules on subject line formatting, conciseness, and clarity across emails and letters (G-1, G-2, G-4).

covers.quote: Use a salutation and sign-off to match the formality
The salutation and sign off should match the level of formality.

rules.quote: At the end of the letter or email, include a sign-off that matches the salutation. Use ‘Yours sincerely’ if you know the person’s name. Use ‘Yours faithfully’ if you do not.
rules.violation_condition: using 'Yours faithfully' when the recipient's name is known, or 'Yours sincerely' when the recipient's name is not known, or omitting a matching sign-off
when: In letters or emails requiring formal sign-offs.
rules.why: Core sign-off convention rule combining salutation/sign-off correspondence (G-2, G-4).

rules.quote: Do not use URLs in emails or letters. Link a word or phrase so the reader is clear about where the link will take them.
rules.violation_condition: a raw URL used as link text in an email or electronic letter instead of linking a descriptive word or phrase
when: In electronic communications (emails or electronic letters). Does not apply to printed letters where URLs must be spelled out.
rules.why: Direct negative command prohibiting raw URLs in digital correspondence (G-2).

rules.quote: Spell out the full URL of any links you use in a letter.
rules.violation_condition: hyperlinked text without the spelled-out full URL in a printed letter
rules.why: Specific rule for print letters contrasting with electronic correspondence (G-2).

rules.quote: Never use an emoji in formal correspondence. Use emojis only when you’re sure they are appropriate, and don’t rely on them for meaning.
rules.specification: Formal correspondence should contain zero emoji characters.
rules.violation_condition: an emoji used in formal correspondence, or used as the sole conveyor of meaning
rules.why: Direct prohibition on emojis in formal writing.

rules.quote: Every email should include a signature block with information about the sender and their organisation.
rules.violation_condition: an email sent without a signature block containing sender and organisation information
rules.why: Clear structural requirement for emails (G-4).
